subject: Sterling Health — evaluation window stagger and acceptance lane (escalation)

Cc: Priya Nair <priya.nair@sterlinghealth.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluation schedule and go-live lanes

Hi Olga / Jonas,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Internal procurement pushed back our acceptance window — legal needs the procurement terms aligned to our master services template before we can sign off on the final acceptance test. That will likely shift our final acceptance date by one week unless we can run a staggered evaluation:

- Week 1 (canary): integration + smoke tests (10 seats)
- Week 2 (parallel): expanded load + dataset eval (prod-like)
- Week 3: final acceptance and sign-off

Two asks: can Redwood support a split acceptance lane so we can ship the canary earlier, and can you share a patched MAP that shows the acceptance gates as separate sign-offs?

Attachments: sterling_map_v1.pdf (draft)

Alec
Director, Digital Ops
Sterling Health
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Alec Thompson <alec.thompson@sterlinghealth.com>, Priya Nair <priya.nair@sterlinghealth.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, Mark Reynolds <mark.reynolds@procureco.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation schedule and go-live lanes

Alec — thanks for flagging. We can absolutely support a staggered acceptance. High level proposal attached and key constraints below.

Summary (short):
- Canary lane: same-day provisioning, basic telemetry, limited KV quota. Goal: ship early business value for 10 seats.
- Parallel lane: additional data syncs, extended token caps, full tracing — target start +7 days.
- Final sign-off: a focused runbook that captures the canary outcomes + explicit acceptance criteria for the big lane.

Constraints / risks (please note):
- Procurement redlines to SOW may block any work that touches data retention beyond customer-controlled retention periods. Legal sign-off is gating for the Parallel lane.
- SLA modifications (we can offer a temporary throughput cap for Canary; any increase requires Dedicated capacity approval).

Action items:
1) Mark — please provide a one-page procurement summary to Priya outlining the single change items (see attached redlines).
2) Jonas — I’ll send a revised MAP PDF that splits the acceptance gates and includes the canary KPIs.
3) Alec/Priya — confirm you can accept canary conditions in writing by EOD Monday so we can stand up the canary on Tuesday.

Attachments: sterling_map_v1.pdf (annotated), procurement_terms_redline.pdf (redline)

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation schedule and go-live lanes / procurement note

Quick note from procurement: we can accept the proposed SOW redline if Sterling agrees to the following conditional items —

- Limited data retention exception (customer-controlled) for the evaluation period only; revert to standard retention on final contract sign-off.
- Trial SLA: Redwood provides monitoring but not full SLA credits for Canary week.
- Cost hold: Canary capacity costs to be invoiced at trial rate; final pricing will be applied on parallel lane kickoff unless signed.

I’ve attached a one-page summary (sla_matrix.xlsx) that maps the trial behaviour to the final SLA. If Sterling can sign the limited exception, legal can expedite the finalization and the parallel lane can start on schedule.

[attachment: sla_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 24 KB)]

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 15:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Evaluation schedule and go-live lanes — Canary commitment and escalation note

Alec / Priya — following up after procurement’s note. To keep the overall close timeline from slipping further I propose:

Plan (finalized):
1) Canary stand-up (Tue 2027-09-21): 10 seats, production-like routing, monitoring enabled. Acceptance criteria for Canary:
   - 95% of inference calls < 220ms P95
   - No functional regressions on the evaluation prompt set (provided by Sterling)
   - CV < 3% on key scoring metric across test dataset

2) Parallel lane (target start Tue 2027-09-28) conditional on:
   - Written confirmation from Sterling that procurement redline exception is accepted for the evaluation period, OR
   - A signed addendum from Redwood agreeing to data retention boundaries in the SOW.

3) Final acceptance window (one business day after Parallel lane completion).

Escalation note: if procurement cannot accept the temporary exception, we will need to delay the Parallel lane by 7–10 days to accommodate legal negotiation. That shift will push final acceptance beyond the current quarter.

Please confirm the acceptance of the Canary conditions by EOD Monday 20 Sep so we can proceed with provisioning. If we do not get a confirmation, Redwood will hold Canary capacity allocation and we’ll escalate to execs for a decision.

Thanks — I’m available for a quick call if helpful.

Olga Petrov
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
